title: A CRISPR/Cas9-induced blunt-end telomere system in S. pombe reveals RNase H2-dependent RNA primer removal at the terminal Okazaki fragment of lagging telomeres.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unzipped the full Europe PMC supplement (1.43 MB) and read all 16 pages of gkag768_supplemental_file.pdf: it holds 8 schematic figure legends (S1-S8) and 5 tables - Table S1 (2 designed telomere cassette sequences, 254 bp and 260 bp), Table S2 (10 sgRNAs with on-target scores), Tables S3-S5 (about a dozen synthetic oligonucleotide markers used as gel size standards). The other 12 supplement files are GIF/JPG copies of the main figures. No spreadsheet, CSV or sequencing data anywhere in the package.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The measurement results themselves (percent of daughter telomeres that are blunt-ended versus Exo I-sensitive, 33.4% / 16.3% / 49.7%, each n = 3 per group) come from reading the figure legends and results text; those numbers live only in bar charts and Southern blot images, not in any table I could open. Also from text only: the data availability statement, which says everything is 'in the article and in its online supplementary material', i.e. no repository deposit.

a1_downloadable.note: The supplement downloads freely and opened on the first try (1.04 MB PDF, no login). It just contains no data tables - verified by extracting text from all 16 pages.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. There is no outcome column anywhere in the files. The paper's measured quantities (overhang length, fraction of Exo I-sensitive telomere ends) exist only as band positions on Southern blot images and bars in figures, so any label would have to be constructed by digitising gel images - exactly the 'build the thing you are predicting' failure.

a3_inputs_present.note: Sequences are literally present: Table S1 gives the two de novo telomere cassettes, Table S2 the 10 sgRNA protospacers plus PAM, Tables S3-S5 the marker oligonucleotides. Verified in the PDF.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated where numbers exist: lengths in base pairs or nucleotides, sgRNA on-target score in percent, blot quantification as percent of signal with mean plus or minus SEM (standard error of the mean). Read in the PDF and figure legends.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL, and badly. The largest table with any numeric column is Table S2: 10 sgRNAs. The whole study covers roughly 8-10 yeast strains with n = 3 biological replicates each - tens of measurements, versus the ~1,500-row (or ~400 for classification) minimum. Counted directly in the PDF.

a6_fits_laptop.note: The entire supplement is 1.43 MB. Trivially fits; this is the only Part A item that is comfortably satisfied.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Table S2's 10 sgRNAs match the 9 panels described in Supplementary Figure S2 plus the sgRNA15/DA260 strain; the strain list in main-text Table 1 is consistent. No contradictory counts found.

a8_label_provenance.note: FAIL for the one modellable column. The sgRNA 'on-target score' in Table S2 is itself the output of Benchling's published scoring algorithm (stated in the table footnote), so training on it would distil an existing predictor rather than learn biology. The genuinely measured outcome (did a de novo telomere form, yes/no in 7 of 9 strains) is an image-derived judgement with no table.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the paper contains tens of image-derived measurements and no feature/label table, so nothing could be trained or honestly evaluated.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use guide RNA sequence to predict whether CRISPR cutting creates a stable new chromosome end in fission yeast.
plain_idea.train_on: The only candidate examples are the 10 guide RNA (short targeting sequence that tells the Cas9 cutting enzyme where to cut) protospacer sequences in Supplementary Table S2, each about 20 letters long, plus the surrounding telomere repeat context. Ten examples, verified by counting rows in the PDF.
plain_idea.predict: Whether inducing Cas9 at that site produces a detectable new telomere, judged by eye from the appearance of a 106 base-pair band on a Southern blot (a gel-based DNA detection method). Seven of nine tested guides worked, per the figure legend.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Nothing here is worthwhile at this size; the project was considered only because the paper reports near single-nucleotide-resolution end structures, which would be valuable training data if they existed as a table rather than as gel images.

ml_idea: No viable idea. The nearest thing would be predicting Cas9 guide efficiency or telomere-end processing outcome from sequence, but this paper supplies 10 guides and a few dozen blot quantifications, and those quantifications are not in any machine-readable file.

effort.compute_note: Sizes are measured, not estimated: the whole supplement zip is 1.43 MB and the PDF 1.04 MB. No training time is estimable because no trainable table exists.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open the supplementary PDF and count the rows in its largest numeric table - it is 10 (Table S2, sgRNAs). That took five minutes and killed the project.

verdict_reason: A classic small-scale wet-lab mechanism paper: the entire 'data' is one 16-page PDF of figure legends, two designed telomere sequences, 10 guide RNAs and a dozen marker oligonucleotides, with no repository deposit. Fails A2 (the outcome exists only as bands on gel images and bars in charts, so the label would have to be digitised into existence), A5 (10 rows in the largest numeric table; roughly 8-10 strains at n = 3 replicates overall) and A8 (the one numeric column, sgRNA on-target score, is another algorithm's prediction). The biology is elegant and the conclusion about RNase H2 removing the last RNA primer is a real advance, but there is nothing here a model could be trained on.
